sample: 142 native-grid boundary-only runs with a valid exact reference and a finite productive method-v4 lower-column control.
question: Do existing Rayleigh candidate diagnostics rank the risk of lower-column change when an accepted higher boundary is used? This is diagnostic association only; no threshold or predictive model is fitted.

within_measurement_wavelength_spearman_s.interpretation: Within-case associations are weak and inconsistent in sign across events. Pooled correlations are confounded by regime and probe altitude and must not be treated as a predictive law.

interpretation: Existing shape QA, SNR, diagnostic cost and path completeness do not consistently rank lower-column sensitivity to a higher boundary across heterogeneous observations.

Some pooled associations are counter-intuitive: better/lower shape cost or higher SNR can coexist with larger lower-column changes because the diagnostics characterize signal shape/precision rather than the aerosol-free boundary assumption.
The result argues against solving P5.4 by merely reweighting the current candidate cost.
decision: Treat physical validity of beta_aer(ref)=0 as a distinct unresolved boundary-condition problem. Do not create a composite Rayleigh score or tuned threshold from these associations.
